GRADE 6 MATHEMATICS — TERM 1 EXAM

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Time: 56 minutes

INSTRUCTIONS
1. Answer all questions.
2. Use neat handwriting.
2. For multiple choice, write the correct letter only.
3. For short answers, write clearly in the spaces provided.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A: Multiple Choice

1. About Whole Numbers at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. use place value and total value of digits up to millions in real life,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

2. About Whole Numbers using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. use numbers up to millions in symbols in real life,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

3. About Whole Numbers when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. read and write numbers up to 100,000 in words in real life,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

5. About Multiplication at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. multiply up to a 4-digit number by a 2-digit number in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication completely.
   C. Multiplication is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication.

6. About Multiplication using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. estimate products by rounding off numbers being multiplied to the nearest ten in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication completely.
   C. Multiplication is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication.

7. About Multiplication when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. make patterns involving multiplication of numbers not exceeding 1,000 in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication completely.
   C. Multiplication is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication.

9. About Division at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. divide up to a 4-digit number by up to a 3-digit number where the dividend is greater than the divisor in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

10. About Division using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. estimate quotients by rounding off the dividend and divisor to the nearest ten in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

11. About Division when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. perform combined operations involving addition, subtraction, multiplication and division up to 3-digit number,
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

13. About Fractions at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. add fractions using LCM in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

14. About Fractions using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. subtract fractions using LCM in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

15. About Fractions when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. add mixed numbers in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

17. About Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. Explain the meaning of Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa using a Kenyan example.
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa completely.
   C. Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa.

18. About Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. Practise Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa at school and at home.
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa completely.
   C. Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa.

19. About Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa helps learners in daily life in Kenya.
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa completely.
   C. Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa.

21. About Decimals at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. Explain the meaning of Decimals using a Kenyan example.
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

22. About Decimals using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. Practise Decimals at school and at home.
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

23. About Decimals when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. Decimals helps learners in daily life in Kenya.
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

25. About Inequalities at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. Explain the meaning of Inequalities using a Kenyan example.
   B. Learners should ignore Inequalities completely.
   C. Inequalities is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Inequalities.

26. About Inequalities using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. Practise Inequalities at school and at home.
   B. Learners should ignore Inequalities completely.
   C. Inequalities is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Inequalities.

27. About Inequalities when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. Inequalities helps learners in daily life in Kenya.
   B. Learners should ignore Inequalities completely.
   C. Inequalities is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Inequalities.

SECTION B: Short Answers

4. Give two examples of how you can use Whole Numbers at the market in your county.

8. Give two examples of how you can use Multiplication at the market in your county.

12. Give two examples of how you can use Division at the market in your county.

16. Give two examples of how you can use Fractions at the market in your county.

20. Give two examples of how you can use Decimals 12 1.6 Inequalities 8 2.0 Measurement 2.1 Length 14 2.2 Area 6 2.3 Capa at the market in your county.

24. Give two examples of how you can use Decimals at the market in your county.

28. Give two examples of how you can use Inequalities at the market in your county.
